checkpoints.description: [1/6] Plan Iris: a pure additive-color beam engine, twelve verified chambers, static browser UI, local launcher, and a Play-page deployment contract

impact_assessment.why: The AegeanWorks Play catalog offers two browser puzzles; a third original title about additive color mixing gives visitors a distinct mechanic, a zero-install game, and a new showcase for the platform's static-build pipeline.
impact_assessment.benefits: A complete offline-capable browser puzzle with deterministic engine and solver tests, frozen levels with equal-par solutions, versioned progress, generated audio, and a documented website contract; no runtime dependencies and no backend.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: new project plus a future third Play-catalog entry; dependency: none beyond Node 20 for tests and tooling; concurrency: the AegeanWorks website playable integration may be uncommitted; state: localStorage progress, media review stamps and copied build digests.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Build and test the engine and solver before the UI, freeze every level with a verified equal-par solution, keep runtime files under index.html and src/assets, and run the project and website gates before any commit or publish.

checkpoints.description: [1/2] Add a GitHub Actions workflow that runs the Node tests, the level-parity checker and the UI inventory on Node 22 and 24, plus the browser dogfood on 22. [2/2] Push and confirm the workflow is green.

impact_assessment.why: The game is published and synced by the website, but its own repository had no CI, so a broken engine, level or UI contract could reach master without a failing check.
impact_assessment.benefits: Every push and pull request now proves the 73 tests, the true-minimum par for all twelve chambers, the UI hook inventory and a real browser solve before the website sync can pick the commit up.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: the workflow must keep working on a clean runner with no install step; dependency: Node 22/24 and the runner's Chrome; concurrency: the website live workflow checks out the same master; state: none.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Use only zero-dependency commands already verified locally, let the dogfood skip when no browser exists, run the same steps locally, and watch the first GitHub run before calling it done.

checkpoints.description: [1/1] Add Node 20, the declared engines floor, to the CI matrix and verify the suite and level checker there.

impact_assessment.why: package.json promises Node 20 or newer, but CI only proved 22 and 24; a regression on the oldest supported runtime could reach master.
impact_assessment.benefits: The matrix now tests every declared major from the floor upward, so the README prerequisite and the actual CI agree.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: one matrix line; dependency: GitHub's Node 20 action support; concurrency: none; state: none.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Run the suite and the level checker under Node 20 locally, then let CI prove the matrix and keep the browser dogfood on Node 22.
